P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No. There are no currency restrictions in the UAE. The dirham has been pegged to the US dollar at AED 3.6725 since 1997.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates Country Commercial Guide — Trade Financing
sources.quote: There are no currency restrictions in the UAE, and residents and non-residents are entitled to hold fully convertible offshore or onshore bank accounts in the UAE or overseas in dirhams or in foreign currency.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates Country Commercial Guide — Trade Financing
sources.quote: The midpoint between the official buying and selling rate for the dirham has been fixed at AED 3.6725 per 1 USD since 1997.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Residents and non-residents may hold fully convertible accounts in dirhams or foreign currency, onshore or overseas.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates Country Commercial Guide — Trade Financing
sources.quote: There are no currency restrictions in the UAE, and residents and non-residents are entitled to hold fully convertible offshore or onshore bank accounts in the UAE or overseas in dirhams or in foreign currency.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Freelancers usually work under a freelance permit or licence from a free zone or emirate authority, or as a sole establishment with a mainland trade licence. Free-zone options include Dubai Development Authority/GoFreelance, Expo City Dubai, twofour54, RAKEZ, Ajman and Fujairah Creative City. Costs vary widely: Dubai Development Authority Dh7,500 excluding visa; Expo City Dubai Dh9,000 per year including a new employment visa; Ajman Dh6,000. Some permits come with a residence visa.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Official TIN description supplied by United Arab Emirates to the OECD: "The United Arab Emirates does not issue Tax Identification Numbers (″TINs″). Therefore, TINs are not automatically issued for Individuals and Entities. The United Arab Emirates issues Tax Residency Certificate s (″TRCs″) (also known as Tax Domicile Certificates) upon application of an eligible individual or entity based on the applicable Double Taxation Treaty. The TRCs are valid for one year and do not carry a TIN." How a freelancer applies (forms, online portal, fees) was not captured.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: There is no personal income tax on employment or investment income. Natural persons conducting a business in the UAE, including freelancers, fall under Corporate Tax once their business turnover exceeds AED 1 million in a calendar year: 0% on the first AED 375,000 of taxable income (profit) and 9% above. Small-business relief for revenue up to AED 3 million is available through tax periods ending in 2026 but requires registration and filing.

sources.quote: Under the UAE CT Law, natural persons who conduct a business or business activity in the United Arab Emirates will be subject to UAE CT at 9% where the total turnover derived from such business or business activity exceeds 1 million UAE dirham (AED).

sources.title: UAE corporate tax: Natural persons and threshold for taxable turnover
sources.quote: The tax rate for natural persons is zero up to AED375,000 in taxable income, with a 9 percent rate applying to amounts exceeding this threshold.

sources.quote: Natural persons (individuals) engaged in business or business activity in the UAE — including freelancers operating under a freelance permit or license — are subject to corporate tax only when gross turnover exceeds AED 1 million in a calendar year.

L3_income_tax_foreign.notes: TRAP: once over AED 1m, registration and returns are required even if relief makes tax zero. FTA/Cabinet Decision 49/2023 text not captured.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 5%. Resident businesses must register above AED 375,000 of taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies (voluntary from AED 187,500). Services exported outside the GCC VAT states are zero-rated where the recipient is outside the UAE; a recipient with only a short-term presence of under a month, not connected with the supply, counts as outside.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates - Corporate - Other taxes
sources.quote: For UAE resident businesses, the mandatory VAT registration threshold is AED 375,000 and the voluntary registration threshold is AED 187,500.

sources.title: United Arab Emirates - Corporate - Other taxes
sources.quote: The 0% VAT rate applies to goods and services exported outside the VAT-implementing Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states, international transportation, the supply of crude oil/natural gas, the first supply of residential real estate, and some specific areas, such as health care and education.

sources.quote: Amounts that can count towards the threshold generally include: Standard-rated taxable supplies subject to VAT at 5% Zero-rated supplies, including qualifying exports

L4_vat_gst.notes: Zero-rated exports count toward the AED 375k threshold (Hawksford).

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL) was issued on 26 September 2021. It is GDPR-like, with access, rectification, deletion and objection rights, and applies to processing of data of UAE residents. Compliance starts six months after its Executive Regulations are issued, and their status was not confirmed. DIFC and ADGM free zones have their own data-protection laws.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (6) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (7) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
